content.1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications:
Steven Edward Boggs is an American experimental astrophysicist (b. 1969 or 1970) with a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (1998) [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[0]] [3]. He currently holds a Professor of Astronomy & Astrophysics appointment at UC San Diego (Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics), where his faculty profile and email "seboggs@ucsd.edu" appear [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[1]] [17]. His CV identifies him as: "Steven Boggs is a professor of Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of California, San Diego. His research is focused on high-energy astrophysics, in particular the development of novel gamma-ray and X-ray instruments with an emphasis on high-resolution spectroscopy. He led the successful NCT and COSI suborbital balloon payloads on six flight campaigns from the US" [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[2]] [73].

He additionally retains a research appointment at the UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory (SSL): the SSL directory lists him as "Steven Boggs, Professor, Email: boggs@berkeley.edu, Phone: 5106434129, 7 Gauss Way, Berkeley" under "Astrophysics & Exoplanets Research" [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[3]] [57]. The Space Physics Research Group at UCB/SSL lists "Steven Boggs, Professor of Physics, Space Sciences Laboratory" with a curriculum vitae and awards/ honors list [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[4]] [58].

**Career timeline:**
- Ph.D. UC Berkeley 1998.
- 2001-2013: UC Berkeley faculty; Associate Director, Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory.
- 2013-2016: Chair, UC Berkeley Department of Physics.
- 2016/2017-2023: Dean of the Division of Physical Sciences at UCSD; returned to research afterwards.
- Source: [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[5]] [1], [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[0]] [3].

**Implication**: The lead's "space sciences lab" reference matches UC Berkeley SSL, where he retains a residual appointment tied to the COSI program. The lead's listed email "sboggs@ucsd.edu" coincides with his UCSD A&A affiliation and personal page.

**Disambiguation check**: Three other "Steven Boggs" / "Steve Boggs" returned by Vespa LinkedIn are unrelated: (a) UCSD Library/ Dean Steven Boggs (administrative; reappointment document from UCSD library.depositcollection) - different person [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[6]] [9]; (b) Steve Boggs, IEEE Dielectrics & Electrical Insulation Society (died July 2018) [1_identity_and_affiliation_verifications[7]] [5]; (c) LinkedIn-only namesakes - "Skill builder at Necco" (Charleston), "Managing Partner Grant, Millman & Johnson P.C." (Novi, Michigan), "Welder/Life Time Drummer" (East Liverpool, Ohio), and Retired Fire Chief (Mississippi). None match the astrophysicist profile.

content.7_synthesis:
**Comparative analysis along three dimensions**:
- **Mechanism**: The most distinctive signal for Steven Edward Boggs (the astrophysicist) is the COSI-APRA balloon PI role at UC Berkeley SSL, coexisting with a UCSD A&A professorship plus a recent decade of senior administration. The COSI-SMEX satellite PI is John Tomsick. -> Distinguishing PI vs PI solos out the right Steven Boggs among namesakes.
- **Scope**: His scientific scope (compact objects, gamma-ray spectroscopy, supernova nucleosynthesis) matches the lead's "nuclear astrophysics" and "balloon instruments" prompts directly.
- **Trade-offs**: The COSI mission - level funding and the still-unsearched research-grant line items look different. Mission-budget claims about the ~$145M belong to COSI as a NASA SMEX, not as a personal grant.
- **Evidence base**: Strongest evidence: Wikipedia, Grokipedia, GitHub CV, UCSD profiles, SSL profile, LinkedIn canonical. Weaker evidence: NASA APRA and NSF awards (no public hits). Weakest: 2026 HERC posting (supervisor not confirmed as Boggs).
- **Time horizon**: 2024-2026 window covered; SSX launch scheduled for 2027; postdoc cycles likely Q1 2027.

**Convergence / divergence observation**: Two related but distinct PIs - Boggs as APRA balloon PI inside the same group, and Tomsick as SMEX satellite PI - is a normal pattern when a lab supports multiple missions. Without name disambiguation, a recruiter risk is conflating Tomsick's postdocs with Boggs's. The COSI SSL paper trail helps consolidate them.

**Holistic recommendation**: The Steven Boggs in the lead matches Steven Edward Boggs at UC San Diego (with a UC Berkeley SSL gravitational project tie) with high confidence. Treat COSI mission budget events as separate from personal research grants; verify personal grants through UCSD/UC Berkeley Office-of-Research Awards directories before quoting any amount. Use the closed UCSD postdoc (PI Boggs) and the closed COSI postdoc (PI Tomsick) as evidence of group activity 2024-2025. Monitor UCSD A&A / UC Berkeley SSL Job pages for the next posting cycle, projected late 2026 to mid 2027.
